unit.why: A single framed narrative: R. Zelig reports R. Meir's account of travelling with the Besht to Brody, where the Besht gave away all his money and assured him they would not lack.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מר' זעליג דק"ק לעטשוב שהלך
stories.summary_en: R. Meir tells R. Zelig how the Besht took him along to Brody, received a gold coin from a rich man there, and gave it all away to the men of the Klaus and to the poor; when the worried Meir protested that they had no money left for expenses, the Besht said they need not worry while he lived, and he indeed brought money home.

quotes: והי' יושב אצל הרב וסיפר לפניו
tags.why: The tale is framed as R. Meir telling R. Zelig while they sat together.
The story turns on the Besht's journey to Brody and his stay at an inn.
The Besht gives the whole gift to the men of the Klaus and to the poor.
The point of the story is the Besht's generosity and his trust in God.

quotes: כל זמן שאני חי אין לנו מה לדאוג
tags.why: The Besht's assurance that they would not lack is fulfilled.

quotes: שאמר שראה השכינה שורה על הקלוז
tags.why: The Besht sees the Shekhinah resting on the Klaus.

quotes: שאמר שראה השכינה שורה על הקלוז
tags.why: A supernatural sight seen while awake.
The Brody study hall (the Klaus) is where the two men wait and is central to the gift.

quotes: נמס לבי בקרבי כי ידעתי שאין לו אפילו פ"א
tags.why: R. Meir is anxious about their lack of money.
R. Zelig lodges with a shochet, but only in the frame.

quotes: ואמר מאיר שב עמי על העגלה
tags.why: R. Meir accompanies the Besht as an attendant and disciple and questions his conduct.

quotes: ואני ראיתי שתם הכסף ביד הבעש"ט
tags.why: The Besht readily gives away all his money despite having none.

quotes: תדע נאמנה כל זמן שאני חי אין לנו מה לדאוג
tags.why: Reliance on the tzaddik's living presence as a guarantee of provision.

missing_concepts: the Klaus of Brody as a holy group of scholars
